Build the project, then run it: execute the produced native_sim binary for a host target, or flash a hardware target (native)

Usage: tan.exe run [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --flash
          Program the board after building (hardware targets only). Required opt-in: without it, `run` on a hardware project builds and reports but never flashes. Ignored for a native_sim/host target, which always runs the produced binary and never flashes

      --project <PATH>
          Project root (defaults to current directory)

      --board-yaml <PATH>
          Explicit board.yaml path (overrides project resolution)

      --core <CORE_ID>
          With `--flash`, flash only the slice with this `core_id` (forwarded verbatim to the native flash path's `--core`)

      --sdk-root <PATH>
          alp-sdk checkout root

      --target <EMIT>
          Generation target (e.g. zephyr-conf, dts-overlay, cmake-args, yocto-conf)

      --all
          Run command against all relevant targets

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - text: Human-readable text (default)
          - json: Machine-readable JSON envelope
          
          [default: text]

      --verbose
          Emit additional diagnostic detail

      --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

      --no-color
          Disable ANSI color in text output

      --non-interactive
          Never prompt. A command with a documented default takes it (`tan init` scaffolds `zephyr-app` into `.`); one without fails instead of asking (`tan scaffold` needs `--name`). The same rule applies unasked when stdin or stderr is not a terminal — piped, redirected, or a CI runner

      --ci
          CI mode: implies non-interactive and disables color

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

Build the project natively: consume the SDK's emitted build plan, materialise its files, then run each per-core slice's command directly

Usage: tan.exe build [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --plan
          Show the build plan (consumed from the SDK's `--emit build-plan`) and exit without building

      --project <PATH>
          Project root (defaults to current directory)

      --board-yaml <PATH>
          Explicit board.yaml path (overrides project resolution)

      --plan-from <FILE>
          Read the build plan from a JSON file instead of invoking the SDK. Implies `--plan`. Use this to consume `alp_orchestrate.py --emit build-plan` output instead of the live emit (which is the default plan source)

      --materialise
          Materialise the plan: write its generated files (shared artefacts + per-slice config) to disk under the build root, instead of just showing the plan. With no `--plan-from`, the plan is fetched live from the SDK

      --sdk-root <PATH>
          alp-sdk checkout root

      --native
          Build natively: consume the plan, materialise its files, then run each slice's command (`west` / `bitbake` / `cmake`) sequentially. This is the default; the flag is kept as an explicit opt-in

      --target <EMIT>
          Generation target (e.g. zephyr-conf, dts-overlay, cmake-args, yocto-conf)

      --all
          Run command against all relevant targets

      --manifest
          Show the system manifest — the post-build IDE/tool contract (`build/system-manifest.yaml`): per-core slices + ipc + helper MCUs. Without `--manifest-from`, asks the SDK for the projection (`alp_orchestrate.py --emit system-manifest`)

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - text: Human-readable text (default)
          - json: Machine-readable JSON envelope
          
          [default: text]

      --manifest-from <FILE>
          Read the system manifest from a YAML file instead of invoking the SDK (e.g. the `build/system-manifest.yaml` a build already wrote). Implies `--manifest`

      --no-auto-bootstrap
          Never bootstrap implicitly. By default a text-mode build with no Zephyr workspace (or a stale one) runs `tan bootstrap` first, which clones Zephyr + the HALs beside the SDK checkout and takes minutes. Use this to keep `tan build` to building and get the readiness report instead

      --verbose
          Emit additional diagnostic detail

      --pristine
          Force-wipe every slice's build dir before dispatch, regardless of the recorded SDK-switch stamp (tan-cli#163) — the manual counterpart to the automatic sdk-switch-pristine wipe, for a stale build dir the stamp heuristic doesn't (or can't yet) catch. Same wipe, same two safety guards (an explicit `-d`/`--build-dir` in the slice's own command, or a plan cwd outside `build/`): this never touches a dir tan can't vouch for, same as the automatic path. A slice the wipe declines — for either guard, or because the dir was never configured — says so on the envelope and in text (`build.pristine-skipped`, tan-cli#183), so "pristine" never silently means "incremental"

      --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

      --no-color
          Disable ANSI color in text output

      --non-interactive
          Never prompt. A command with a documented default takes it (`tan init` scaffolds `zephyr-app` into `.`); one without fails instead of asking (`tan scaffold` needs `--name`). The same rule applies unasked when stdin or stderr is not a terminal — piped, redirected, or a CI runner

      --ci
          CI mode: implies non-interactive and disables color

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

Flash every slice + helper MCU from `build/system-manifest.yaml` onto the device in `boot_order` (native)

Usage: tan.exe flash [OPTIONS] [APP_PATH]

Arguments:
  [APP_PATH]
          Application source directory (default: `.`, the current directory). `build_root` defaults to `<app_path>/build`. Optional positional (the unified app-path convention: `tan flash` from the app dir needs no argument, matching the retired Python `app_path` default)
          
          [default: .]

Options:
      --build-root <PATH>
          Override the build root holding `system-manifest.yaml` (default: `<app_path>/build`)

      --project <PATH>
          Project root (defaults to current directory)

      --board-yaml <PATH>
          Explicit board.yaml path (overrides project resolution)

      --dry-run
          Print the flash command each backend WOULD run and return ok without spawning; also bypasses the required-tool PATH gate

      --core <CORE_ID>
          Flash only the slice with this `core_id` (skips every other slice AND all helpers)

      --sdk-root <PATH>
          alp-sdk checkout root

      --helper <NAME>
          Flash only the helper MCU with this name (skips ALL slices and every other helper)

      --target <EMIT>
          Generation target (e.g. zephyr-conf, dts-overlay, cmake-args, yocto-conf)

      --all
          Run command against all relevant targets

      --skip-missing-tools
          When a backend's required tools are all absent from PATH, warn + skip the entry instead of failing it. No effect under `--dry-run`

      --format <FORMAT>
          Output format

          Possible values:
          - text: Human-readable text (default)
          - json: Machine-readable JSON envelope
          
          [default: text]

      --verbose
          Emit additional diagnostic detail

      --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

      --no-color
          Disable ANSI color in text output

      --non-interactive
